findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently overwrites the first in Ruby
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading: defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at line 145. Any existing caller passing separate width and height (5 positional arguments including opts) will now raise ArgumentError, breaking thumbnail/downsize paths that use the old signature. The two signatures must be merged into one method that handles both forms.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle as WxH dimensions
findings.body: `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which passes `dimensions` to `gifsicle --resize-fit`. The new caller in UploadsController passes `"80%"`, but gifsicle expects a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` geometry, not a percentage, so animated GIFs that exceed the size limit will fail to be downsized (or error out) while the upload loop keeps retrying, and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected or stored unshrunk.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and proceeds with an oversized upload
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value and never verifies the result after the loop. If `convert` fails (unsupported format such as SVG, corrupt image, missing tool) or 5 reductions of 20% are not enough, execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized tempfile, producing an opaque validation failure instead of a meaningful error, after wasting up to 5 external-process invocations.

findings.title: In-place ImageMagick conversion reads and writes the same file
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` runs `convert <path>[0] ... <same path>`. ImageMagick is not guaranteed to handle in-place conversion safely: the output file can be truncated/created before the input is fully read, corrupting the upload (especially on failure mid-write, the original tempfile is destroyed). Convert to a separate temp file and atomically replace the original only on success.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured per-type size settings
findings.body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a constant `10 * 1024` breaks the admin-configured contract for both images and attachments: sites that lowered `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` will now accept files client-side that the server/model then rejects (or expensively downsizes), and sites that raised the limit above 10 MB will have valid uploads blocked client-side. The same regression is repeated for the 413 handler at line 246, which also now always reports 10 MB even for attachment uploads.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10 MB remote-download and unbounded direct-upload downsizing invite resource exhaustion
findings.body: The API URL branch now always downloads up to 10 megabytes regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and the new downsize block runs ImageMagick (up to 5 passes) on any image tempfile above the limit with no upper bound on its incoming size. A user can supply a very large/high-resolution image (within the web server's body limit) and force repeated decompression/conversion of it in the deferred job, consuming disproportionate CPU/memory; previously the download was capped at the configured image limit and oversized files were rejected cheaply by validation.
